unverified.detail: `key` must name a withdrawal key already set up in Kraken's own address book (see `withdraw_addresses`); calling with an unregistered `key` just returns an API error, not a meaningful example. The account's real `withdraw_addresses` currently has exactly one entry ('Deribit' -> an ETH address), which is not the address `client.toml`'s `[policy.permissions].withdraw_addresses` pre-approves (a different `0xE089aB95D28aCA5804a2F99c2cc259A88d3Be799`). The policy-approved address has not been added as a withdrawal key on the account, so there is no in-policy `key` to call this with yet. Needs that address registered as a withdrawal key (a manual/write-adjacent account step) before this can be captured.

spec.description: Retrieve fee information about a potential withdrawal for a particular asset, key, and amount. Requires the `Funds permissions - Query` and `Funds permissions - Withdraw` API key permissions.

key.description: Withdrawal key name, as set up on the account.

response.title: WithdrawalInfoFrame
response.description: Wire frame; the generated method returns `result`.

error.description: Wire envelope field; see the core.

result.title: WithdrawalInfo
result.description: Fee and limit information for a potential withdrawal.

method.description: Name of the withdrawal method that will be used.

limit.description: Maximum net amount that can be withdrawn right now.

amount.description: Net amount that will be sent, after fees.

fee.description: Amount of fees that will be paid.

notes: Upstream `requestBody` requires `nonce`; dropped from this schema since the core's `authed_request` (`core/transport/http.py`) injects a strictly-increasing nonce into every private call automatically -- it is never a caller-supplied parameter, matching the existing hand-written `deposit_methods(self, asset)` signature, which takes none.
